preferences: AGENT CREATION: Use role_models mapping for provider strings. The format is provider/model where model can contain slashes (e.g. opencode/opencode-go/mimo-v2.5). Do NOT use bare opencode-go/ prefix as provider.
PROVIDER ROUTING: For OpenAI models, route via the codex provider as codex/<model> (e.g. codex/gpt-5.6-sol). MiMo workhorses stay on opencode-go.
impl: model=opencode-go/mimo-v2.5, thinkingOptionId=max, features.auto_accept=true, features.fast_mode=true, modeId=build
ui: provider=claude, model=claude-opus-5, thinkingOptionId=high (limited budget - reserve for copywriting, naming, UX copy, visual design, styling only)
planning: model=claude/claude-opus-5, thinkingOptionId=high (limited budget - reserve for high-value planning only). Fallback to codex/gpt-5.6-sol when claude limits hit.
audit: model=opencode-go/minimax-m3, thinkingOptionId=max (lead reviewer - cross-family contrast from impl). For a second opinion, escalate to codex/gpt-5.6-sol, thinkingOptionId=high.
vision: model=opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 (for image and video input)
mimo-v2.5 is the primary workhorse with effectively unlimited usage. Use it for all impl, research, scheduled, and recurring work.

mimo-v2.5 is also the orchestrator: it decides, synthesizes outputs, and delegates. When a decision needs frontier-model judgment, the orchestrator itself makes the call to codex/gpt-5.6-sol for that one step, then resumes on mimo-v2.5.
Claude budgets are limited. Reserve claude-opus-5 for human-skill work (ui) and high-value planning. Use them only when the task specifically requires their reasoning strength.
For audits and reviews, lead with minimax-m3. Bring in codex/gpt-5.6-sol only as a second opinion when the first review is contested, high-stakes, or needs a different family's judgment.
For committees and second opinions, deliberately use a different model family than the primary agent to get genuine cross-model contrast.
Prefer asynchronous workflows. Set notifyOnFinish=true for all agent-scoped creates. Do not poll for completion.
Use workspace isolation (worktree mode) when running multiple agents in parallel on the same repo to prevent filesystem conflicts.
